newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Rifkind says EU stability pact doesn't apply to UK.
newsitem.headline: Rifkind says EU stability pact doesn't apply to UK.

text.p: British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind said on Monday Britain would not be bound by the planned European Union stability pact linked to the introduction of a single currency.
"We are not going to be bound by it as the chancellor has already said," Rifkind told reporters as he entered an EU foreign ministers' meeting.
He was referring to British Chancellor of the Exchequer (finance minister) Kenneth Clarke who is due to make a statement on the EU single currency to the British parliament on Monday.

His remarks came a day after European finance ministers and central bank governors agreed to let the lira rejoin the European exchange rate mechanism (ERM), a move hailed by the Italian government as a major step toward joining the single currency.

Rifkind said that British MPs concerns about the single currency, such as those expressed by John Redwood, the right-wing challenger to the leadership of the ruling conservative party, could be answered.
"I think Mr. Redwood's concern can be easily answered," Rifkind said.
